muc.title: Choose-your-own-adventure books
muc.text: Remember the books where the end of the page said: to open the door, turn to page ten; to run away, turn to page twenty?

muc.title: Branching scenarios
muc.text: In education, this is called a branching scenario. Each choice you make opens up a different outcome.

muc.title: Don't memorize, see it happen
muc.text: You don't memorize rules, you see the consequences for yourself. What you say to a customer, and whether they're happy or walk away, sticks with you for a long time.

muc.title: The story writes itself
muc.text: Writing a branching scenario used to take a whole week. Now AI is the storyteller: it makes up what happens based on exactly what you choose.

muc.title: A coffee shop
muc.text: For example: you're the manager of a coffee shop, and a customer complains their drink order was wrong. Four choices appear, you pick one, the customer reacts, and the story continues.

muc.title: It can teach a lot
muc.text: It works for teaching customer service, team management, workplace safety, even teaching your kids how to say no to strangers.

muc.title: A role-playing game
muc.text: Message AI: make a role-playing game that teaches me to handle customer complaints. Give four choices each turn, and after five turns, score me and explain.

muc.title: Simulations with buttons
muc.text: All the simulations so far have been text. Part five: ask AI to build a real simulation with buttons and sliders.
